name: Doro Wat
description: Ethiopia's famous spicy chicken stew simmered in berbere sauce with hard-boiled eggs.
steps: Marinate chicken with lemon juice.
Cook onions low and slow in niter kibbeh.
Add berbere, garlic, and ginger; cook until deep red.
Add chicken and simmer until tender.
Add eggs and serve with injera.

name: Shiro Wat
description: Smooth, spiced chickpea-flour stew — an everyday vegetarian favorite across Ethiopia.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons niter kibbeh Ethiopian spiced clarified butter
steps: Heat a heavy stockpot over medium heat.
Add pureed onions; sauté until dry and lightly colored, about 4–5 minutes.
Stir in oil and berbere; cook 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add tomato and garlic; sauté 2–3 minutes.
Whisk in chickpea flour and 2 cups water until smooth; add remaining ½ cup water if you prefer thinner shiro.
Bring to a simmer, then stir in niter kibbeh, garlic powder, and salt to taste.
Simmer on low 5–10 minutes until flavors combine and oil slightly separates.
Serve with fresh injera.

name: Injera
description: Sourdough flatbread made from teff flour — the base of almost every Habesha meal.
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon active dry yeast (or 1 cup starter)
steps: Mix teff, water, salt, and yeast in a bowl.
Cover and ferment at room temperature for 24–48 hours (or 4–6 hours with yeast).
Whisk batter until thin and pourable.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour a ladleful of batter, swirl to spread thin.
Cook until bubbles form and edges lift (about 2–3 minutes, do not flip).
Remove and stack between towels; serve with shiro.

name: Kitfo
description: Finely minced raw beef mixed with mitmita and niter kibbeh, often served with ayib.
ingredients: 1 lb lean beef (minced or finely chopped)
4 tablespoons niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
steps: Ensure beef is very fresh and finely minced or chopped.
In a bowl, combine beef, niter kibbeh, mitmita, and salt.
Mix thoroughly until butter and spices coat the meat evenly.
Serve immediately with ayib (Ethiopian cottage cheese) and gomen (collard greens), if desired.

name: Firfir
description: Torn injera stir-fried with berbere, onions, and spices — a classic Ethiopian breakfast.
ingredients: 4 cups torn injera (stale or fresh, roughly 2-inch pieces)
2 tablespoons niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced clarified butter)
steps: Heat niter kibbeh in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and berbere; cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in water or stock and bring to a simmer.
Add torn injera pieces and stir well to coat with the sauce.
Cook for 3–5 minutes until the injera softens and absorbs most of the liquid, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt to taste and serve warm.

name: Misir Wat
description: Red lentil stew cooked with berbere and onions until thick and rich.
